instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice in a strainer. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water, bring it to a boil, then cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes and leave the lid on until you serve.
Slice the pork across the grain into thin slices, about 1/8 inch, then cut the slices into bite-size strips.
Chop 4 of the garlic cloves with the stems from half the cilantro bunch. Add the white pepper, then press and smear the pile with the flat of your knife until it's a rough paste.
In a large bowl, mix the pork with the paste, the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar. Use your hands so every piece is coated, then leave it for 15 minutes.

Mince the other 8 garlic cloves. Pour the oil into a 12-inch skillet or a wok, add the garlic, and set it over medium heat. Stir often for 2 to 3 minutes, until the garlic is pale golden. It keeps darkening after it comes out, so don't wait for deep brown.
Lift the garlic out with a slotted spoon onto a plate lined with paper towels and sprinkle it with the salt. Leave the oil in the pan.
Stir the cornstarch into the pork until the pieces have a wet, sticky coating. Turn the heat to medium-high. The oil is ready when a piece of pork sizzles right away.

Add about a third of the pork, spreading the pieces apart so they don't clump. Fry for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, until golden and cooked through, then transfer to a second paper towel plate. Repeat with the other two batches. You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick piece. No thermometer? Cut a thick piece open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Slice the cucumber. Pile the pork on a platter, scatter the crispy garlic over the top, and pull the leaves from the cilantro to scatter over it too.
Taste a piece. If it's flat, sprinkle a pinch more salt over the pork.
Serve with the rice and the sliced cucumber.
method_notes: None of the versions found has a rating on the page, so the lead is the restaurant-style Thai version that fries the pork and tops it with separately fried garlic (thaidata.uk, taken from a Wongnai recipe); the milk in that marinade was left out to keep it dairy-free. The shorter marinade (15 minutes, as in the Bell V Kit and Garlic Shop versions) replaces the 2-hour or overnight rest in the food.com version so the dish stays at 30 minutes. Coriander root is swapped for cilantro stems, and the pork is shallow-fried in batches with a cornstarch coating, as in the Garlic Shop version. The dish is dry by design and no sauce was added. Prep 15 and cook 15 assume the rice goes on first and the pork marinates while the garlic fries.
